title: Embodied AI Industry
question: How can robot demos, technical routes, and real delivery fit into one industry map?
current_answer: A demo, a pilot, and continuous delivery are different kinds of evidence. Start with the task and the person the robot serves, then compare forms, technical routes, and company positions.
gap: Next: confirm the public scope of the full report, review company status, and keep technical routes and real deployments current.

title: Home Robots
question: Which household tasks justify bringing a robot into daily life, and who takes over when it fails?
current_answer: A household task makes sense only when the labor saved exceeds deployment, maintenance, and rescue costs. Platform discussions reveal task leads; they do not prove purchase demand.
gap: Next: manually review samples by household role and task, then add long-term use, takeover frequency, and willingness-to-pay evidence.

title: AI Glasses and Spatial Interaction
question: When does AI deserve to leave the phone and enter a new device on the body or in space?
current_answer: A new device needs a frequent task, an acceptable physical burden, and a job existing devices cannot complete comfortably. Combined corpora reveal scenarios; they cannot replace behavior and adoption evidence.
gap: Next: review samples by device, role, and scenario, then add continuous-wear, real-behavior, and payment evidence.

title: Local AI and Personal Compute
question: Which tasks truly need to run locally, and should they use an existing computer, shared device, or dedicated hardware?
current_answer: First prove that the task must happen locally and continuously. Then compare performance, permissions, maintenance, and human intervention. The existing computer is the default alternative; dedicated hardware must add value across the whole workflow.
gap: Next: compare devices on real workloads and add installation, maintenance, recovery, and long-term-use evidence from non-technical users.

title: AI Video and Creative Tools
question: How do generative models enter professional video workflows that require editing, collaboration, and delivery?
current_answer: The first generation provides a starting point. Professional delivery also needs reliable local edits, timeline control, versioned assets, and collaboration interfaces.
gap: Next: reconcile local and Feishu versions, check product and workflow facts, then decide the main report’s public scope.

title: Agent Systems and Capability Measurement
question: When agents genuinely use software, which actions, outcomes, and value should be recorded?
current_answer: A call, a task, an adopted outcome, and a business gain have different denominators. Context, state, and permissions must also be recorded to explain success or failure.
gap: Next: add real-task benchmarks, cross-product event comparisons, and continuous calibration between specification fields and current implementations.

title: Product Research and Organizational Methods
question: How can evidence about demand, competitors, organizations, and versions support the next decision?
current_answer: Every piece of evidence should name the decision it supports, the responsible owner, and the change that would trigger another review.
gap: Next: add authorized real cases and records of how the methods succeed and fail in different projects.

title: Desktop Digital Manufacturing
question: How does a digital design pass through materials, processes, and equipment states to become a repeatable physical delivery?
current_answer: The design file is only the input. A valid delivery also records material batches, process parameters, equipment state, and inspection results, with traceability across every step.
gap: Next: repair the multidimensional-table archive gap, verify report versions, then decide whether to publish equipment and process comparisons.

title: DJI Alumni Startups and Industry Diffusion
question: When people leave a hardware company for new teams, which capabilities genuinely travel with them?
current_answer: A shared employment history shows association, not capability transfer, equity relationships, or startup success. Research must trace how products, supply chains, and organizational experience enter the new team.
gap: Next: review company status, product changes, and public sources item by item while accounting for sample-selection bias.
